content.content: deccy redo reverts the revert entries undo recorded and is valid while the redo tail holds the operation — while the position is before the marker count. A new operation discards the tail. Redo applies to whole operations only.
content.rationale: Redo is the re-application of the next undone operation rather than a branch: the linear history (kpptprql) keeps the undone markers after the position, so redo is valid exactly while pos < length, and a new operation discards that tail before appending. Whole-operation scope keeps every intermediate state a valid graph.
